findings.claim: The new second setAutoCommit(true) message ('Turning auto-commit back on here commits the open transaction at once, so a later commit() or rollback() has nothing to finish and fails') fires whenever setAutoCommit(true) appears textually before conn.rollback(). For try { ...; conn.commit(); conn.setAutoCommit(true); } catch (SQLException e) { conn.rollback(); throw e; } (verified by running the extracted t3Check in node) the transaction is already committed and rollback() only runs on paths where that line never executed, so the stated reason is false for this placement; the real problem is only that auto-commit is not restored when the transfer fails. Separately, the first message now says 'before the updates run', which is inaccurate when setAutoCommit(true) sits between credit.executeUpdate() and debit.executeUpdate() (credit has already run). Rejecting both placements is fine; the explanations are what mislead.
findings.recommendation: Give the after-commit-in-try case its own message (for example: 'This restores auto-commit only when the transfer succeeds; move it to a finally block so it is also restored after rollback().'), and reword the first message to 'before the second update runs' or back to 'before the transfer is committed'.
